claim_en: שמונים ("eighty") — the Ramah: "ONE alone in the Torah is written plene with vav" — Methuselah's SECOND eighty (5:26, after he begot Lamech), plene with vav and yod; every other Torah eighty (including Methuselah's first, one verse earlier) defective. Minchat Shai calls the six-plene Masorah note "two errors"; SNAPSHOT sides with the Ramah: nine eighty-tokens, exactly one plene, at 5:26.

source: Avodah Zarah 5a:9; Bereshit Rabbah 24:2; Bereshit Rabbah 24:4
claim_en: THE LEDGER OPERATOR IS READ AS A SCHEDULER. סֵפֶר (sefer, 'book') at our 5:1 is read as a registry ALREADY WRITTEN and shown to the first human - 'He showed him each generation and its expositors, its sages, its leaders' - so that 'in Your book all of them are written' means they were written in the book of the first man. From this the chain draws a scheduling claim: THE MESSIANIC KING WILL NOT COME UNTIL ALL THE SOULS IN THE BOOK OF ADAM ARE CREATED. The unit's genealogical ledger is thereby a queue the world drains, and its completion is a precondition for an event outside the corpus.

check.note: A ledger operator read as a work queue whose exhaustion gates a later event.

claim_en: A DISPUTE OVER WHICH VERSE IS THE TORAH'S GREATEST PRINCIPLE, SEATED ON OUR 5:1 - and the seats do not rank it the same way. Ben Azzai holds 'this is the book of the generations of Adam' the great principle; R. Akiva holds 'love your neighbour as yourself'. At the Bereshit Rabbah seat the two are presented level; at the Jerusalem Talmud seat Ben Azzai says our verse is a principle GREATER THAN THAT. The strength of the claim varies between seats, and both forms are carried.

check.note: A dispute whose relative ranking differs between seats - a strength-variance, recorded rather than smoothed.

claim_en: THE PROCREATION MEASURE IS PROVED FROM OUR 5:2. The case-table rule - a man may not neglect procreation unless he has children - is disputed as to the measure, and the House of Hillel's ruling of A MALE AND A FEMALE is proved by citing this verse's own words, 'male and female He created them'. The House of Shammai holds two sons. The same verse yields a further rule: 'whoever has no wife is NOT ADAM, as it is stated: male and female He created them AND CALLED THEIR NAME ADAM' - the shared name read as making the pair the person.

check.note: A canonical case-table row whose stated proof-text is this unit's own verse - a testing-shelf row anchored here.

middah: plain (the procreation measure proved from the verse's own male-and-female — Yevamot 61b)

claim_en: THE LIKENESS-RECAP AT 5:3 IS READ AS A BOUNDARY MARKER WITH A DARK INFERENCE. Because the verse says that at 130 years he begot 'IN HIS LIKENESS, AFTER HIS IMAGE', R. Yirmeyah ben Elazar infers what the verse does not say: until then, NOT after his image - and reads those years as a period under ban in which spirits were begotten. Bereshit Rabbah gives three answers to why 'THESE are descendants and the earlier were not', including that the first three alone stood in the image and that the earlier were the spirits of those 130 years.

check.note: An inference from what the recap verse specifies to what the preceding silence implies.

middah: plain (the inference from what the verse specifies at 130 — not before; Eruvin 18b)

claim_en: A DISPUTE FOUGHT WITH DUELLING VERBAL ANALOGIES ON THE SAME WORD. Our 5:24 says of Chanokh that God TOOK him, and the verb is contested: some argue from the taking of Elijah that he did not die; R. Abbahu answers with a COUNTER verbal analogy from the taking of Ezekiel's wife, where the same verb plainly means death. The chain also records him as capricious - written in the ledger of the wicked, taken 'while in his righteousness' before he could turn. The machine's entry for this generation therefore carries a contested exit rather than a settled one, and the contest is between two applications of one middah.

check.note: Middah E7 (equal decree) deployed by both sides on the same verb - the inference rule itself becoming the battleground.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 25:2; Sanhedrin 113b:3; Tosefta Sotah 10:1; Tosefta Sotah (Lieberman) 10:2
claim_en: THE NAMING AT 5:29 IS BOTH A DISPUTED ETYMOLOGY AND A GENERAL RULE. The name is disputed with the explicit caveat that 'the name is not the exposition': R. Yochanan reads the furrow and the ox obeying again; Reish Lakish the WATERS resting; R. Eliezer the pleasing savour of the later offering. And from the same verse the chain states a rule of the world: 'when a righteous one comes into the world, GOOD comes into the world - as it is stated: THIS ONE WILL COMFORT US', carried at both the Tosefta base and its Babylonian seat.

check.note: A naming operator carrying a three-way etymology dispute and a general rule about righteous arrivals.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 26:3; Bereshit Rabbah 37:7; Sanhedrin 69b:15; Bereshit Rabbah 26:2
claim_en: THE THREE-SONS LIST OF 5:32 IS ORDERED BY RANK, NOT BIRTH - AND THE CHAIN PROVES IT ARITHMETICALLY. Shem is named first though Yefet is the elder, and the ordering is justified by rank: righteous, born circumcised, the Name attached to him, the line of Abraham, the priesthood, the Temple in his territory. The arithmetic is opened rather than credited: Shem reaches a hundred two years after the Flood, so he cannot be the eldest. The chain also asks why this man alone begot at five hundred where the others begot at a hundred or two, and answers that the chronology is DESIGN - so that no child would reach the punishable age of a hundred before the Flood came.

check.note: A list order justified by rank with a supporting computation, opened per credit guard 3 rather than credited unread.
